value.value: may not be in a Comdat

note: One defect, two signatures, exactly the shape the skill's 'any_of' guidance describes. On stable RELEASE binaries (asserts compiled out) the repro reaches LLVM's IR verifier and prints the LITERAL text quoted in the issue -- 'Declaration may not be in a Comdat!\ni32* @"\01?Num@?$Test@$0CK@@@2HA"' -- byte-identical on v1.7.2308 and v1.9.2607 (see out-v1.7.2308.txt, out-v1.9.2607.txt) to the mangled name quoted in the issue body, even though the exit code is plain E_FAIL (0x80004005), which is_internal_failure() correctly treats as an ORDINARY diagnosed error, not a crash -- so this clause must be text-based, not status-based. On this Debug main-debug ground truth, a DIFFERENT, EARLIER Debug-only assert fires first, before the verifier is ever reached: assert(!Old || Old->getCachedLinkage() == D->getCachedLinkage()) in clang::LinkageComputer::getLVForDecl (tools/clang/lib/AST/Decl.cpp:1357), exit 0xE0000001, matched by is_internal_failure() via both the exit code (STATUS_LLVM_ASSERT) and the printed 'Internal compiler error: LLVM Assert' text (see out-main-debug.txt). Continuing past that Debug-only assert under cdb with 'gh' (emulating NDEBUG, i.e. what the Release path takes) shows the compiler then reaches the exact Comdat message quoted above before hitting 'error: LLVM ERROR: Broken module found, compilation aborted!' (manual-case-gh-continue.txt) -- confirming both signatures are the same underlying defect (HLSL's static/global codegen override producing an invalid/uninitialized-looking declaration for a templated static data member), diverging only on whether the unrelated Debug-only linkage-cache assert happens to trip first. Controls: control-nontemplate.hlsl (non-templated struct, same static-member pattern) and control-templateconst.hlsl (templated struct, static CONST member) both --expect no-match and both score no-repro on main-debug, matching the issue's own claim that both of those patterns already work.
